event.title: Manhunt Underway After Deadly Attack at Berlin Pride Event
event.canonical_title: Manhunt Underway After Deadly Attack at Berlin Pride Event
event.summary: A manhunt is ongoing for a 21-year-old suspect following a deadly attack near Berlin's Pride festival, which left one person dead and at least 16 injured. Authorities suspect the incident, involving a van ramming and subsequent stabbings, to be an act of Islamist terrorism. The suspect has been identified and is believed to have connections to extremist groups.

revisions.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride Attack Shot Dead by Police Following Ramming Incident
revisions.summary: A 21-year-old man, identified as the main suspect in a ramming attack during Berlin's Pride celebrations, was shot dead by police. The incident occurred on Saturday night when the suspect drove a minivan into a crowd near the Brandenburg Gate, resulting in one fatality. The attack is being treated as an assault on the LGBTQ+ community, prompting condemnation from officials.
key_facts: Ramming attack occurred near Berlin's Pride celebrations
One person died in the incident
Attack regarded as targeting the LGBTQ+ community

event_overview.title: About Berlin Pride Attack
event_overview.subject: Berlin Pride Attack
event_overview.summary: The Berlin Pride attack refers to a deadly assault in the Tiergarten area of central Berlin on July 25, 2026, during the city’s Christopher Street Day (CSD) weekend. Berlin prosecutors said the suspected attacker allegedly used a rented vehicle and a bladed weapon against people near the event; one woman died and multiple people were injured, with the investigation continuing.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: Authorities place the attack at about 10 p.m. on July 25, 2026, in the Tiergarten area of Berlin, in the vicinity of Christopher Street Day celebrations.

facts.label: Alleged method and casualties
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office said the suspect was alleged to have injured several people with a rented vehicle and a bladed weapon; a woman died that evening and other people were seriously injured.

facts.label: Underlying event
facts.value: Berlin CSD 2026 was the 48th Berlin Christopher Street Day, organized by Berliner CSD e.V.; organizers described it as a demonstration for democracy, diversity and human rights.

facts.label: CSD schedule and format
facts.value: The Pride weekend was scheduled for July 24-25, 2026. Its July 25 demonstration was to begin on Leipziger Straße, proceed via Potsdamer Platz and Nollendorfplatz toward the Victory Column, with programming around the Brandenburg Gate.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office and police described the case as an active investigation and said that detailed public disclosures were limited in order to protect it.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate attack and law-enforcement response on July 26-27, 2026; it does not provide a full account of the broader Berlin CSD program, later legal proceedings, or longer-term security and policy consequences.
